newsitem.title: THAILAND: NAP coalition moves to boost image, form cabinet.
newsitem.headline: NAP coalition moves to boost image, form cabinet.

text.p: The New Aspiration Party (NAP) and its five coalition partners are working to boost their image, form a cabinet and define policies for the next Thai government, analysts said on Tuesday.
The NAP won the most seats -- 125 to 123 for the second-place Democrat Party -- in Sunday's general election and, by tradition, the right to try to form the next government.

On Monday, NAP leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who probably will become the next prime minister, dropped the image-tainted Chart Thai Party of caretaker prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa from the coalition. He replaced it with the Chart Pattana Party of former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan.
Political and economic analysts said investors should now have more confidence in the coalition.

"The image of Chart Pattana party looks better and more acceptable than Chart Thai. Their economic team led by Amnuay (Viravan) is far better than that of the previous government," Paiboon Rajaniyom of Asia Security Trading told Reuters.
The other coalition partners are the Social Action, Prachakorn Thai, Seritham and Muon Chon parties.
Banharn was forced to resign as prime minister and call the election after a bruising no-confidence debate in which he and his party were accused of corruption and mismanagement.
Banharn's administration has been blamed for many of the country's economic woes, including sagging exports and a yawning current account deficit.
Chavalit has made the economy his top priority. He told a news conference he would give Amnuay -- a respected economist -- free rein in managing the economy.

The stock market rose about 3.0 percent to 971.07 by midday on Tuesday after plunging six percent on Monday. Analysts said the rebound was due to improved sentiment regarding the coalition because it did not include Banharn's party.
"Chart Pattana has more capable and more acceptable people, and that can encourage the public and boost investor confidence," said Ramkhamhaeng University political scientist Sukhum Naulsakul.
Chavalit said the coalition had agreed in principle how to assign the cabinet portfolios, but he would not give details.
A party source said the NAP was set to fill 24 of the 49 cabinet posts and would be responsible for the economic and security aspects, including the powerful Interior Ministry.

Chart Pattana, the second-largest coalition member with 52 seats in the 393-member parliament, would get 10 portfolios including the communications, commerce and industry ministries. The smaller partners would be given ministries dealing with social issues.
About five porfolios, mostly in the economic area, would likely go to outside, non-elected experts like Amnuay.

"Currently, representatives from the coalition partners are drafting our policy by merging that of all the parties. It will be short with a clear time frame and be easily implemented policy," Chavalit told reporters at parliament on Tuesday.
He said Tuesday's cabinet meeting, the last for Banharn's administration, would discuss when parliament would resume and the next government would be sworn in.

Although the palace issues a royal decree setting the date for parliament to reconvene, it is done in consultation with politicians. Officials say it will likely be on November 27, and the parliament president would be chosen the next day.

The parliament president submits the name of the new prime minister to King Bhumibol Adulyadej for approval, after which the premier submits his list of cabinet ministers for royal approval. Officials expect this to take place in early December.
